Mr. Nayanar was not a member of the Assembly at the time of swearing in. Elected on October 13, 1996 from Tellicherry constituency in a by-election. Resignation submitted on May 13, 2001, and was asked to continue until alternate arrangements are made. BACK
prose: In the 1996 election to the 140-seat Kerala Legislative Assembly, the Left Democratic Front (LDF) emerged largest with 80 seats, against 59 for the UDF (1 to others/independents). Turnout was 71.26% of 20,633,069 electors.
By vote share, the LDF polled 44.78% and the UDF 44.84%, with the NDA on 5.53%. A total of 1,341 candidates contested the 140 seats.
Compared with 1991, the LDF gained 32 seats (from 48 to 80); the UDF moved from 92 to 59. Power changed hands from the UDF.
The closest contest was Kunnathunad, won by M. P. VARGHESE (CPM) over T. H. MUSTAPHA (INCI) by just 60 votes. The largest margin was M. P. M. ISHAQ KURIKKAL in Manjeri (28,655 votes).
E.K. Nayanar headed the Council of Ministers that followed.
